chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from Salih ibn Abi Hammad, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamza, from Safwan, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, who said:
I asked Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about the Aqeeqa upon the solvent and the insolvent, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'There is nothing upon the one who cannot find (the means).'

key_terms.الْعَقِيقَةِ: Aqeeqa, the sacrificial animal offered upon the birth of a child
key_terms.الْمُوسِرِ: The solvent, one who has sufficient financial means
key_terms.لَا يَجِدُ: Cannot find, lacking the means or capacity
key_terms.وَالْمُعْسِرِ: The insolvent, one who lacks sufficient financial means

ai.seo_question: Is Aqeeqa obligatory for everyone or only for those who can afford it?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam Al-Reza (peace be upon him) clarifies that the Aqeeqa is a recommended act (Sunnah) rather than a strict obligation (Wajib), specifically exempting those who lack the financial means. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle of ease (*Yusr*) in worship, ensuring that financial hardship does not become a burden for the parents of a newborn.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Muhammad, from Salih Bin Abu Hammad, from Muhammad Bin Abu Hamza, from Safwan, from Is’haq Bin Ammar who said,
‘I asked Abu Al-Hassanasws about the Aqeeqa upon the (financially) solvent and the insolvent. So heasws said: ‘There is nothing upon the one who cannot find’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Muhammad has narrated from Salih ibn abu Hammad from Muhammad ibn abu Hamzah from Safwan from Ishaq ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following: “
I once asked abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about ‘Aqiqah for one who is affluent and one who is poor. He (the Imam) said, ’It is not necessary for one who cannot find anything.’”
